cases.name: checked-arithmetic
cases.description: Forge checks solc/EVM checked and unchecked arithmetic behavior; pinned solc and the common checker reject nested unchecked blocks; Lean checks the paired Solidity source-interpreter witnesses.

cases.name: rational-constants

cases.name: packed-storage
cases.description: Forge checks solc/EVM top-level, struct-field, and fixed-array packed storage writes through source-visible reads; Lean imports the same source contract from solc AST and checks the abstract source storage words plus returned values.

evals.label: importedTopLevelPackedValues
evals.expr:
(do
  let contract := SolidCore.Solidity.SolcAstImport.PackedStorage.importedContract
  let state ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.Examples.checkedOwnCallState 128 contract "setTopLevel" SolidCore.Solidity.Source.State.empty []
  let read ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedInput.ownCall 64 contract (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallTarget.name "readTopLevel") state []
  match read with
  | SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.returned _ [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word a, SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word b, SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word c, SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.int s, SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word d] =>
      Except.ok
        (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq a 0x12 &&
          SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq b 0x3456 &&
          SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq c 1 &&
          SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq s (SolidCore.Solidity.Shared.signedToWord (-1)) &&
          SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq d 9 &&
          SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq (state.loadSlot 0) 0xff01345612 &&
          SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq (state.loadSlot 1) 9)
  | _ => Except.ok false)

  let structRead ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedInput.ownCall 64 contract (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallTarget.name "readStruct") state []

      Except.ok
        (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq a 0x12 &&
          SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq b 0x3456 &&
          SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq c 1 &&
          SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq s (SolidCore.Solidity.Shared.signedToWord (-1)) &&
          SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq d 9 &&
          SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq first 0xaa &&
          SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq second 0xbb &&
          SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq third 0xcc &&
          SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq fourth 0xdd &&

cases.name: reentrancy-adoption
cases.description: Forge runs real reentering callees (attacker reenters the victim; a value-refunding callee; a child constructor calling back) and traces the victim's adopted self-account changes; Lean models each as a PostDelta on the outgoing-call/create responder row (openworld/postworld Stage 3) and checks the victim observes the adopted storage/balance/transient/create-callback change after the call, including a reentrant ill-encoded word read totally through Stage 0 (bool truthy, enum Panic 0x21) and the balance lane pinning that adoption, not the A2 debit, is authoritative.

evals.label: reentrantStorageWrite
evals.expr:
(do
  let program ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedInput.program SolidCore.Solidity.SolcAstImport.ReentrancyAdoption.importedSourceUnit
  let contract ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedProgram.contract program "ReentrancyAdoptionVictim"
  let callRow : SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallResult := { kind := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallKind.call, target := 0, calldata := (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordToBytesBE SolidCore.Solidity.Source.selectorBytes (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ABI.selectorFromSignature "notify()")), value := 0, gas? := none, success := true, output := [] }
  let delta : SolidCore.Solidity.Source.PostDelta := { selfStorageWrites := [(0, 42)] }
  let responder : SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ScriptedResponder := [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.OracleRow.callWithPost callRow delta]
  let result ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedContract.callFunctionWithContextUnderResponder 64 responder contract "pull" contract.core.context SolidCore.Solidity.Source.State.empty []
  match result with
  | SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.returned st [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word v] =>
      let read ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedContract.callFunctionWithContextUnderResponder 64 [] contract "x" contract.core.context st []
      (match read with
       | SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.returned _ [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word xv] => Except.ok (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq v 42 && SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq xv 42)
       | _ => Except.ok false)
  | _ => Except.ok false)

evals.label: reentrantIllEncodedThenRead
evals.expr:
(do
  let program ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedInput.program SolidCore.Solidity.SolcAstImport.ReentrancyAdoption.importedSourceUnit
  let contract ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedProgram.contract program "ReentrancyAdoptionVictim"
  let callRow : SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallResult := { kind := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallKind.call, target := 0, calldata := (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordToBytesBE SolidCore.Solidity.Source.selectorBytes (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ABI.selectorFromSignature "notify()")), value := 0, gas? := none, success := true, output := [] }
  let delta : SolidCore.Solidity.Source.PostDelta := { selfStorageWrites := [(1, 2), (3, 7)] }
  let responder : SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ScriptedResponder := [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.OracleRow.callWithPost callRow delta]
  let result ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedContract.callFunctionWithContextUnderResponder 64 responder contract "pull" contract.core.context SolidCore.Solidity.Source.State.empty []
  match result with
  | SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.returned st _ =>
      let flagRead ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedContract.callFunctionWithContextUnderResponder 64 [] contract "flag" contract.core.context st []
      let flagOk := (match flagRead with | SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.returned _ [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word v] => SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq v 1 | _ => false)
      let choiceRead ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedContract.callFunctionWithContextUnderResponder 64 [] contract "choice" contract.core.context st []
      let choiceOk := (match choiceRead with | SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.reverted _ (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.RevertData.panic code) => SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq code 0x21 | _ => false)
      Except.ok (flagOk && choiceOk)
  | _ => Except.ok false)

cases.name: source-declarations
cases.description: Forge checks solc/EVM source-unit and contract-local declarations; pinned solc and the common checker reject bad source-unit pragmas, modifier/error overloading, duplicate event ABI signatures, inherited declaration shadowing, event static-form errors, declaration data-location errors, deprecated constructor visibility errors, callable header/override errors, fallback/receive header errors, state-mutability violations, and same-block duplicate locals while accepting nested-block local shadowing; Lean imports the whole solc AST and checks free declarations, local declarations, using, enums, structs, arrays, constructors, fallback/receive overrides, event static forms, and public getters as source semantics.

evals.label: importedSourceDeclarationsRunAndGetters

  let selector := fun signature => SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ABI.encodeSelector (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.ABI.selectorFromSignature signature)
  let dirtyArray := encodeWord 32 ++ encodeWord 1 ++ encodeWord 256
  let dirtyPair := encodeWord 7 ++ encodeWord 256
  let call := fun signature args => SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedContract.callCalldata 256 contract SolidCore.Solidity.Source.State.empty (selector signature ++ args)
  let memArray <- call "memArrayLength(uint8[])" dirtyArray
  let cdArray <- call "cdArrayLength(uint8[])" dirtyArray
  let memPair <- call "memPairFirst((uint8,uint8))" dirtyPair
  let cdPair <- call "cdPairFirst((uint8,uint8))" dirtyPair
  Except.ok (!memArray.success && memArray.output == [] && cdArray.success && cdArray.output == encodeWord 1 && !memPair.success && memPair.output == [] && cdPair.success && cdPair.output == encodeWord 7))

cases.name: packed-ternary-width
cases.description: Forge and the imported Lean interpreter compare solc's abi.encodePacked width for a conditional operand: abi.encodePacked(cond ? a : b) with a uint8 then-branch and a uint16 else-branch packs the result using the ternary's common type (uint16 -> 2 bytes) in both branches, pinned via keccak256 of the packed bytes.

cases.name: completeness-boundaries
cases.description: Completeness boundaries C1-C4 (2026-07-08). Pinned solc 0.8.35 and this repo's typechecker both REJECT: (C1) `string.length` (must use `bytes(s).length`), (C2) `type(ConcreteContract).interfaceId` (only interface/abstract are non-deployable and expose interfaceId), (C3) `abi.encodePacked` of an array whose element is dynamically sized (`bytes[]`,`string[]`). Both still ACCEPT the neighbors: `bytes(s).length` and `uint[].length`; `type(Interface).interfaceId` and `type(Abstract).interfaceId`; `abi.encodePacked(uint[])`. C4: constant `%` with a negative operand is VALID and folds to the truncated remainder (sign of dividend): (-7)%3==-1, 7%(-3)==1, (-7)%(-3)==-1 (was over-rejected). solc source: Types.cpp ArrayType::nativeMembers (string has no length), Types.cpp:4271-4285 (type(C) member set gated on deployability), packed-mode nested-dynamic rejection, and constant-expression `%` folding.

cases.name: hash-precompile-builtins

evals.label: sha256DigestsMatchEvm
evals.expr:
(do
  let source := SolidCore.Solidity.SolcAstImport.HashPrecompiles.importedSourceUnit
  let program ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedInput.program source
  let contract ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedProgram.contract program "HashPrecompilesHarnessTarget"
  let ctx := contract.core.context
  let word32 : List Nat :=
    [0x61,0x62,0x63,0x64,0x65,0x66,0x67,0x68,0x69,0x6a,0x6b,0x6c,0x6d,0x6e,0x6f,0x70,
     0x71,0x72,0x73,0x74,0x75,0x76,0x77,0x78,0x79,0x7a,0x30,0x31,0x32,0x33,0x34,0x35]
  let long40 : List Nat := word32 ++ [0x36,0x37,0x38,0x39,0x30,0x31,0x32,0x33]
  let mk := fun (kind : SolidCore.Solidity.Shared.Precompile.Kind) (data : List Nat) (digest : SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Word) =>
    ({ kind := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.LowLevelCallKind.staticcall
       target := SolidCore.Solidity.Shared.Precompile.address kind
       calldata := data

  let run := fun (fn : String) (kind : SolidCore.Solidity.Shared.Precompile.Kind) (data : List Nat) (expected : SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Word) => do

    | _ => Except.ok false
  let sha := SolidCore.Solidity.Shared.Precompile.Kind.sha256
  let s0 ← run "sha256Of" sha [] 0xe3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855
  let s1 ← run "sha256Of" sha [1,2,3] 0x039058c6f2c0cb492c533b0a4d14ef77cc0f78abccced5287d84a1a2011cfb81
  let s2 ← run "sha256Of" sha word32 0x653bb1245e828fcda4fa53fcd5a3def5bd7654e651f54b4132b73d74e64435c4
  let s3 ← run "sha256Of" sha long40 0x2fa2c189076e20488be2d1da4af97695cff36f38a0b528347b600f3e3912b353
  Except.ok (s0 && s1 && s2 && s3))

cases.name: block-env-builtins
cases.description: Forge pins BLOCKHASH (blockhash(uint)) and BLOBHASH (blobhash(uint), EIP-4844) against Foundry-EVM with block.number fixed at 1000 via vm.roll: current/future/older-than-256 blocks return 0, the number-1 and number-256 boundary blocks return the deterministic Foundry hashes, and blobhash returns 0 for a non-blob tx. Lean imports the same solc AST and drives the interpreter under a context whose blockHashes map carries the SAME ground-truth hashes plus non-zero decoys at the out-of-window slots, so the interpreter's availability-window predicate (not a map miss) is what forces 0.

evals.label: blockhashBlobhashMatchEvm
evals.expr:
(do
  let source := SolidCore.Solidity.SolcAstImport.BlockEnvBuiltins.importedSourceUnit

        , (744, 0x7468eddb0720a03646876d25045fa535478c57a57b912a197efd90e8d667279c)
        , (1000, 0xdead1000)
        , (1001, 0xdead1001)
        , (743,  0xdead0743) ] } }

  let bhBoundary ← run "blockHashOf" 744  0x7468eddb0720a03646876d25045fa535478c57a57b912a197efd90e8d667279c

cases.name: acceptance-boundaries
cases.description: Acceptance boundaries G2-G10 (2026-07-08). Pinned solc 0.8.35 and this typechecker both REJECT: (G2) msg.value in a non-payable public/external function (TypeError 5887; internal/library/payable exempt), (G3) ==/!= on a reference type bytes/string/array/mapping/struct/UDVT (TypeError 2271), (G4) a compile-time out-of-bounds constant index on a bytesN or fixed-size array (TypeError 1859/3383), (G5) a bare return; with a non-empty (even named) return list (TypeError 6777), (G6) super.f() resolving to an abstract/unimplemented base function (TypeError 9582), (G7) a qualified emit X.g() whose member callee is not an event (TypeError 9292), (G9) an inline array literal of a mapping element type (invalid memory type), and (G10) msg.data inside a receive function (TypeError 7139). Both still ACCEPT the neighbors: msg.value in a payable/internal function; == on address/uint; an in-bounds or dynamic index; a value-carrying/implicit return; super.f() to an implemented base; simple and member-form emits of a real event; an inline array of a value type; and msg.data in an ordinary/fallback function. G8: revert E(...) where a contract-level non-error member (function or state var) shadows a free error E (TypeError 1885); neighbors — a genuine contract error and an unshadowed free error — still revert.

cases.name: acceptance-boundaries-round2
cases.description: Round-2 acceptance boundaries (2026-07-08) from docs/solc-implementation-divergences-2.md. Pinned solc 0.8.35 and this typechecker both REJECT: (E1) a NON-rational immutable read (keccak256- or constant-ref-initialized) inside a pure function (TypeError 2527; only a RationalNumber initializer stays pure), (O1) a duplicate contract in an override(A,A) list (error 4520), and (PT1) a constant whose value cyclically depends on itself (error 6161). Both still ACCEPT the neighbors on the Lean side: the same immutable read in a view function and a numeric-literal / constant-arithmetic immutable read in pure; the legitimate diamond override(A,B); a non-cyclic constant chain. E2 (over-reject fix): this.f.selector in a pure function is now ACCEPTED while this.f() stays a pure-violation. AE1 confirmed already-handled: abi.encodePacked(bytes[]/string[]) is rejected while encodePacked(uint[]) is accepted.

cases.name: ternary-literal-mobile-type
cases.description: Forge checks solc/EVM conditional-of-literals typing: `(t ? 63 : 255)` carries the ternary's common (mobile) type uint8 (not uint256), assignable to a uint8 local, implicitly widening to uint256, and its `+1` overflows uint8 -> Panic 0x11; larger literals raise the common type to uint16. Lean imports the same contract from the solc AST and checks the source ternary mobile-type behavior (G15).

cases.name: nested-tuple-assignment
cases.description: Forge checks solc/EVM nested tuple assignment `((a, b), c) = ((x, y), z)` (and `(a, (b, c)) = …`): the RHS tuple is evaluated once, left-to-right, and destructured against the nested target tree in lockstep, a swap `((a,b),c)=((b,c),a)` reads the RHS into temps first, and a nested hole `((a,),c)=…` evaluates then discards its component. solc accepts these; Solidus formerly over-rejected them (flat tuple LHS). Lean imports the same contract from the solc AST and checks source nested-tuple assignment behavior (G13).

cases.name: storage-array-copy-convert
cases.description: Forge checks solc/EVM copy assignment into a DYNAMIC storage array with a wider-unsigned element source and/or a differing length (`uint16[] = uint8[]`, `uint256[] = uint8[]`, longer-source clear): the dest is resized to the source length, elements are widened per-element, and a longer old tail is zero-filled. solc accepts these; Solidus formerly over-rejected the whole array-copy family. Lean imports the same contract from the solc AST and checks the copied values (G14).

cases.name: narrow-udvt-arithmetic

evals.expr:
(do
  let src := SolidCore.Solidity.SolcAstImport.NarrowUdvtArithmetic.importedSourceUnit
  let st := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.State.empty
  let w := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word
  let i := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.int

      | SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.returned _ [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.int v] => Except.ok (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq v expected)
      | _ => Except.ok false

  let a2 ← callPanic 32 "addU8" [w 200, w 100] 0x11
  let a3 ← callPanic 32 "addI8" [i 100, i 100] 0x11
  let a4 ← callPanic 32 "subI8" [i (SolidCore.Solidity.Shared.signedToWord (-100)), i 100] 0x11
  let a5 ← callWord 32 "addI8" [i (SolidCore.Solidity.Shared.signedToWord (-100)), i 50] (SolidCore.Solidity.Shared.signedToWord (-50))
  let a6 ← callWord 32 "addU8Unchecked" [w 200, w 100] 44
  let a7 ← callPanic 32 "addU8Operator" [w 200, w 100] 0x11

cases.name: nested-tuple-internal-call
cases.description: Forge checks solc/EVM nested tuple assignment whose RHS contains INTERNAL function calls: a multi-return call filling a nested target `((a,b),c)=(foo(),bar())` (foo returns a 2-tuple), scalar calls in nested RHS positions `((a,b),c)=((g(),h()),k())`, and a hole whose component call still runs. The RHS is evaluated once left-to-right (side effects in that order) then destructured. solc accepts these; Solidus formerly over-rejected (nested elaboration could not hoist internal calls). Lean imports the same contract from the solc AST and runs the source semantics (R1).

cases.name: storage-array-copy-signed-fixed
cases.description: Forge checks solc/EVM storage-array copy for the shapes G14 deferred: SIGNED element widening (int8[] -> int16[], sign-extend each element, never overflows) and FIXED-length destinations (T[N] = S[M], N >= M) including signed, with the M..N tail padded 0. solc accepts these (ArrayType::isImplicitlyConvertibleTo); Solidus formerly over-rejected (canImplicitlyConvert had no array arm, and the fixed-dest write could not pad). Lean imports the same contract from the solc AST and runs the source semantics (R2).

cases.name: narrow-arith-widened
cases.description: Forge checks solc/EVM narrow-integer arithmetic assigned/returned at a WIDER type: solc computes the op at the operands' common type, so a narrow overflow Panics 0x11 even though the result is widened. uint8+uint8 / uint8*uint8 / int8+int8 returned as uint16/int16 panic on operand-width overflow; a non-overflowing add widens; an explicitly-256-bit-widened add (uint256(a)+uint256(b)) does NOT panic. Solidus formerly cleaned only at the wider target width and silently produced the fitting wide value (the G15-noted narrow-arithmetic-widened gap). Lean imports the same contract from the solc AST.

cases.name: cf2-revert-pruning
cases.description: CF2 (2026-07-08, docs/DECISIONS.md): solc's ControlFlowRevertPruner prunes the edge after a call to an always-reverting callee, so the storage-pointer-return definite-assignment check (error 3464) runs on the pruned CFG. Solidus now computes an always-reverts fixpoint and treats a call to such a callee as terminating, ACCEPTING pick(bool) returns (uint256[] storage p) whose only obligation-unmet path runs through the always-reverting helper alwaysReverts(); importedContractAccepted confirms the fix on the Lean typechecker. Forge (real EVM, pinned-solc compiled) is the value ground truth: the non-reverting path returns xs = [11,22,33] via pickLength/pickAt. (The Lean source Core interpreter does not lower an internal function that returns a storage pointer, a pre-existing limitation orthogonal to CF2, so the value is checked by Forge only.) Pinned solc 0.8.35 REJECTS the sound neighbors — a genuinely-unassigned path, a sometimes-reverting helper, a require(false) helper (require is not an always-revert terminator), and an external this.boom() callee — and the Lean witnesses confirm Solidus rejects them too.

cases.name: packed-nested-static-array

Forge/pinned-solc pin the packed layout and the two source rejections; Lean witnesses pin the accept/reject typecheck boundary and the packed byte layout.

cases.name: using-for-global-nonudvt
cases.description: Forge and imported Lean execute `using {f, g} for S global;` on a STRUCT (a non-UDVT user-defined target), resolving `s.doubled()` and `s.plus(y)` through the file-level global directive (finding UF1); the imported source also carries `using {f} for E global;` on an ENUM, whose acceptance is pinned via importedContractAccepted and the common checker. Pinned solc rejects an operator binding on a struct target, a `global` directive on a built-in type, a mixed-parameter operator function (UF2), and a duplicate operator binding for one operator+type (UF3); the common checker matches via usingForGlobalNonUdvtDisciplineMatches.

evals.label: importedGlobalUsingMemberValues
evals.expr:
(do
  let src := SolidCore.Solidity.SolcAstImport.UsingForGlobalNonUdvt.importedSourceUnit
  let st := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.State.empty
  let w := SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word
  let chk : Nat → String → List SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value → Nat → Except SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.TypeError Bool :=
    fun fuel fn args expected => do
      let r ← SolidCore.Solidity.TypeCheck.CheckedInput.callContract fuel src "UsingForGlobalNonUdvt" (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallTarget.name fn) st args
      match r with
      | SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.returned _ [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.word v] => Except.ok (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq v expected)
      | SolidCore.Solidity.Source.CallResult.returned _ [SolidCore.Solidity.Source.Value.int v] => Except.ok (SolidCore.Solidity.Source.wordEq v expected)
      | _ => Except.ok false
  let d ← chk 64 "computeDoubled" [w 21] 42
  let pl ← chk 64 "computePlus" [w 21, w 8] 29
  Except.ok (d && pl))
